transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I keep hearing voices coming from the call-light speaker and the hallway vents. They tell me which patient records have been changed, clear as if someone’s standing right beside me, even when the unit is quiet and nobody else hears anything.
How long have you been hearing these voices?
About two months now—since they asked me to help lead the wound-care documentation rollout.
Over these past two months, how has your mood been?

Some days I feel really up, like I’m finally awake and I’m supposed to fix everything at work. But if my husband or one of the nurses tells me to slow down, I get irritated fast—like they’re getting in the way of something important.
Do you still hear the voices on days when your mood feels completely normal?

No. I never had the voices—or the hidden messages in the charts—before I got so wound up about the rollout. They started after I was barely sleeping, working nonstop, and feeling like it was all on me to fix the place.
Before this began two months ago, have you ever had a time in your life when you felt unusually energized or wound up like this?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of another time like this before these past two months.
Have you ever had a time in the past when you felt deeply down, depressed, or lost interest in everyday things for a couple of weeks or more?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had bad days like anybody, but I can’t remember being depressed for weeks at a time or losing interest in everything.
Have you been using any recreational drugs, prescription medications, or other substances over the past few months?
I’m not really sure what all counts. I haven’t noticed anything specific like that.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions or noticed any new physical health problems recently?
No, I haven’t been diagnosed with any medical problems that I know of, and I haven’t noticed any new physical health issues recently.

Psychotic symptoms only occur in the context of the affective episode, and there is no prior history of affective episodes, confirming a single manic episode with psychotic symptoms (F30.2).

delusions of reference / persecution (hidden messages in charts)
